text:
**Short answer:** For a typical full-size fridge, look for a station with about **1,500 Wh or more** of capacity and a **surge rating of at least 1,300 W**. That covers roughly a day. For two days, you need about 2,800 Wh.

**Three things to check**

1. **Surge (startup) watts:** The compressor draws a brief spike when it starts. Sources estimate 900 to 1,200 W for a typical fridge, and a larger model may need 1,500 to 2,400 W. [HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/) and [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator) use a 1,300 W allowance. If the station's surge rating is below the fridge's startup draw, it will shut off at the first start, no matter how much battery it has. Check your fridge's label or manual for its own figure.
2. **Running watts:** Usually 100 to 250 W while the compressor runs. Almost any station rated around 1,000 W or more handles this easily. [BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage)
3. **Watt-hours:** The compressor only runs about 30 to 40% of the time, so the fridge uses much less energy than its label suggests. An ENERGY STAR 18 cu ft fridge uses about 1,000 Wh per day, or about 1,400 Wh once you allow for inverter losses and headroom. [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator) Your fridge's yellow EnergyGuide label gives its annual kWh. Divide that by 8,760 to get average watts.

**Options from the search results**

| Station | Capacity | Surge / AC output | Fit | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bluetti AC180P | 1,440 Wh | 2,700 W surge | About one day | [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/power-station-for-a-refrigerator) |
| Bluetti AC180 | 1,152 Wh | 2,700 W peak | About 17 to 19 hours, a bit short of a full day | [BlackBox Supplies](https://www.blackboxsupplies.com/guides/what-size-power-station-to-run-a-refrigerator-in-a-power-outage) |
| Bluetti AC200L | 2,048 Wh | 2,400 W continuous, 3,600 W power lifting | About 33 hours per HomeGrid's estimate | [HomeGrid HQ](https://www.homegridhq.com/watts/fridge/) |
| Anker SOLIX S2000 | 2,010 Wh | 3,000 W peak | Roughly 1.5 to 2 days, with low idle draw | [Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/portable-power-station-for-refrigerator) |

The AC200L is a good pick if you want room to spare and possible expansion later. It can take expansion batteries up to 8 kWh, and its sources include a [Dealectric listing](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac200l) showing a $899 price with code AFF5OFF for $854.05, tested October 21, 2026. Dealectric earns a commission on purchases made through that link, and prices change, so check the checkout price yourself.

**Tips**

- Keep the fridge door closed. Sources say food is generally unsafe after about 4 hours above 40°F.
- Choose pure sine wave output. It is standard on the LiFePO4 units above, and it is best for compressor motors.
- Plug the fridge directly into the station, not into a power strip or extension cord.
- If the fridge's startup draw is unknown, check the manual or ask the manufacturer before relying on a specific model.
